Projects.title: James Furniture
desc: In 2015, I designed and developed the James Furniture e-commerce website using WordPress, creating a fully functional online store for the client. Leveraging WooCommerce as the core platform, I implemented product catalogs, secure payment gateways, and an intuitive checkout process to ensure a seamless customer experience. The responsive design adapted flawlessly across desktop and mobile devices, while performance optimization techniques like caching and image compression improved loading speeds.

I customized WordPress themes to align with James Furniture's brand identity, incorporating high-quality product galleries and customer review systems. Additional features included inventory management, promotional discount modules, and integration with shipping calculators. This project strengthened my expertise in WordPress development, UI/UX best practices, and translating business requirements into technical solutions for small-to-medium enterprises.

Projects.title: Galler-AI
desc: Galler-ai is an innovative web platform that harnesses the power of OpenAI to generate stunning images based on user prompts. Built using React for a dynamic user interface and Node.js for robust server-side operations, the site provides a seamless experience for users looking to explore AI-generated artwork.

Projects.title: Bestinform
desc: Bestinform is a robust booking platform focused on European travelers, providing fast and accurate reports for hotel and restaurant bookings. Built with Angular and Spring Boot, it highlights my full-stack development skills, ensuring a seamless user experience. The platform stands out for its reliability and efficiency, making it a go-to resource for travelers planning their journeys.

Projects.title: Drivemond
desc: Created an all-in-one solution for taxi service management, including passenger and driver apps. Integrated real-time tracking, payment, and admin dashboard features.

Projects.title: IIPM.ie
desc: From April 2025 to March 2026, I developed IIPM.ie through an Upwork engagement for the Irish Institute of Pensions Management, collaborating with its Australia-based agency and Daniel Steven. The project began as a set of WordPress landing pages, drawing on my previous WordPress experience. As the requirements and business workflows expanded, I reorganized the product structure and implemented the larger platform in PHP, following the client's technology requirements, with PostgreSQL for data storage.

The members portal supports both individual and organisational memberships. Organisational members register through an existing organisation, while applicants complete onboarding and qualification requirements before activation. Active members submit monthly course progress for administrative review, pay annual membership fees, and receive downloadable PDF certificates after completing the year's requirements.

The admin portal provides statistical dashboards for monitoring membership, onboarding, qualifications, payments, and course progress. Administrators can account for approved leave or absences when calculating programme timelines and issue annual certificates to eligible members. The work passed through two feedback stages—the agency and the final client—and replaced several manual documentation processes with automated workflows.

Projects.title: SafeSchoolz
desc: From June 2024 to June 2025, I worked with David Gray, VP of Grays Communications in Los Angeles, on SafeSchoolz—a safety platform designed to detect firearms and help communicate potential incidents to first responders. After I delivered an initial signal-triggering Android prototype, I took responsibility for building the Media Pipe and Aegis applications and integrating them with the existing HeroEyez portal.

Media Pipe performs firearm detection from an Android device or IP camera feed and sends an alert to Aegis. Aegis receives the alert with screenshots and a one-minute evidence clip, initiates a Twilio-powered call workflow, and forwards the incident to HeroEyez. The .NET-based HeroEyez portal stores evidence and incident records, displays the event location through Google Maps, and gives monitoring teams the information needed to coordinate a response.

The main technical challenge was improving object-detection accuracy while keeping inference practical on edge devices. I initially evaluated YOLO, then moved to TensorFlow Lite to better fit mobile hardware constraints. I trained and tested the model with more than 10,000 firearm images from Roboflow and custom-captured samples, then completed the alert flow between Media Pipe and Aegis. The application was deployed in June 2025, although broader commercial rollout was later paused because of market and regulatory constraints.

Projects.title: Equity Funding Source
desc: From April to July 2026, I built Equity Funding Source for a mortgage-loan broker based in Los Angeles. I used Preact for a lightweight frontend and Bun for the backend, allowing the application to remain fast while supporting the workflows required by borrowers, lenders, and administrators. AI-assisted development with Codex helped accelerate implementation and iteration without sacrificing the stability of the final system.

The project required a detailed analysis of United States mortgage and private-lending workflows, including the forms and information exchanged throughout the loan process. I deployed the platform on Cloudflare, using Workers for server-side execution, D1 for relational data, Durable Objects for real-time messaging, and R2 for document storage. The result is a streamlined platform that supports borrower applications, lender collaboration, administrative oversight, and secure document handling.
